bib.title: KARL: Knowledge Agents via Reinforcement Learning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "KARL: Knowledge Agents via Reinforcement Learning", Databricks AI Research. First author Jonathan D. Chang (correspondence j.chang@databricks.com); last authors Wen Sun, Michael Bendersky, Jonathan Frankle. arXiv:2603.05218v1 [cs.AI], dated March 6, 2026 on the cover and 5 Mar 2026 in the arXiv stamp. Preprint, no venue.
COVERAGE: 77 of 77 pages extracted (217,272 chars). Pages 1-32 (body and references) read in full. Appendix pages 33-40 (authors, cost/latency method, latency tables), 46-47, 52-53, 70-72 and 77 read in full. Appendix C dataset examples, D prompts/filter examples (pp 41-45, 48-51, 54-58) and E/G case-study traces (pp 59-69, 73-76) were only skimmed via the page index, because they are example text and model traces with no results. The charts in Figs 8-14 and 17-18 came out as garbled glyphs, but their numbers are restated in the text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Headline: with no test-time compute, KARL is on par with Claude Sonnet 4.5. With parallel thinking it matches Claude 4.6 Opus. Bears on notes 05, 06, 11.
 number: KARLBench total 58.9 (KARL), 67.5 (KARL par. N=10), 68.1 (N=20). Opus 4.6 scores 67.5, Sonnet 4.5 58.6, GLM 4.5 Air 52.6.
 setup: base model GLM 4.5 Air, multi-task RL on BrowseComp-Plus plus TREC-Biogen, 2 OAPL iterations. KARLBench has six tasks, and Claude/GPT scores are the best across reasoning efforts. The paper reports no seeds and no confidence intervals for scores. Single run per cell.
 quote: "KARL (par.N= 10) 67.5 86.7 58.6 84.5 59.7 47.8 77.1 62.7 67.5" (Table 4); "Without any test-time compute, KARL achieves parity with Claude Sonnet 4.5 with high reasoning effort" (p15)
2. Generalization: multi-task RL beats multi-expert SFT distillation out of distribution. Notes 05, 06.
 number: SFT-distilled in-distribution 69.1→75.3 with parallel thinking, OOD only 59.4→59.6. KARL reaches 62.7 OOD with N=10.
 quote: "On in-distribution tasks, SFT benefits substantially from parallel sampling (69.1→ 75.3), yet on out-of-distribution tasks the gains are negligible (59.4→ 59.6)." (p16)
 Single-task experts do not transfer to each other's task: KARL-TREC gets 42.2 on BrowseComp-Plus, and KARL-BCP gets 68.0 on TREC-Biogen (Table 4).
3. Cost and latency. Notes 10, 05.
 number: under $0.10 per query single-call. About 33% lower cost than Opus 4.6 at matched quality. About 47% lower latency than Opus 4.6 at N=10. Cheaper than base GLM 4.5 Air while scoring 6+ points higher.
 setup: the cost is token counts times artificialanalysis.ai prices, 4 generations per prompt. Latency is wall-clock time to first answer token on an 8×H200 vLLM node, tensor parallel 8, concurrency 1. It uses 5 prompts × 30 trajectories per benchmark and 3 splits. Mean effective latency is 14,615 ms for KARL, 13,758 ms for GLM 4.5 Air, 32,753 ms for Sonnet 4.6, 30,566 ms for Opus 4.6 and 82,748 ms for GPT 5.2 (App. B, pp 35-40). Training cost (GPU hours, hyperparameters) is not reported. Searches for "GPU hour", "learning rate" and "batch size" found nothing.
 quote: "the single-call KARL achieves competitive scores at under $0.10 per query, the lowest cost of any model above 55 points." (p16)
4. Method: OAPL, iterative large-batch off-policy RL, loss min Σ (β ln π(y|x)/πref(y|x) − (r − V̂*(x)))², with V̂* estimated from a group of rollouts. Needs no clipped importance weights, data deletion or router replay. Max 3 iterations. Notes 10, 08. Cited as concurrent work (Ritter et al. 2026), so the paper gives no head-to-head comparison against GRPO.
 quote: "without requiring heuristics such as clipped importance weighting, data deletion, or router replay that were thought to be necessary for stabilizing online GRPO" (p2)
5. Iteration gains and "beyond sharpening" evidence. Notes 08, 05.
 number: KARL-TREC on TREC-Biogen goes 66.0 → 76.0 → 82.0 → 85.0 over 3 iterations. After iteration 3, max@1 equals base max@8, and max@2 exceeds base max@16. On BrowseComp-Plus training prompts, 37.2% of unsolved became partial and 33.3% of partial became solved.
 quote: "its max@2 already exceeds the base GLM 4.5 Air's max@16" (p18)
6. Agentic synthesis pipeline (note 06). A question-answer synthesizer agent explores the corpus with vector search. A dedup agent removes near-duplicates of eval questions. 8 solver rollouts per question are used for pass-rate filtering, which drops all-correct and all-wrong items. A quality-filter agent then screens for ambiguity and wrong answers. The synthesis and solver models are the model being trained at each iteration. On BrowseComp-Plus Iter. 1, 13,882 synthetic questions end as 1,218 training prompts (Fig. 37). Table 3 gives 1,218 and 1,336 BrowseComp-Plus prompts and 6,270 and 11,371 TREC-Biogen prompts for iterations 1 and 2. Seeding synthesis with documents gave a 25% increase in document coverage. The eval-set questions are used as few-shot seeds for TREC-Biogen, with dedup against them. The synthesis seeds for BrowseComp-Plus come from the 600-question validation split.
7. Reward and environment ablations (KARL-BCP, BrowseComp-Plus, note 07). The reward is outcome-only nugget-based, from LLM judges.
 number: removing compression drops the score from 0.570 to 0.389. Swapping the embedder (Qwen3-Embedding-8B to GTE-large hybrid) gives 0.568. Retrieving 40 docs per search degrades sharply. Performance scales with the step horizon from 10 to 200 and plateaus through 400. Compression is trained end-to-end in RL. With KARL-BCP as the compressor and GLM 4.5 Air searching, the score rises from 0.44 to 0.54.
 quote: "Removing the compression tool leads to a substantial drop in accuracy (0.570→ 0.389)" (p19)
8. Test-time compute (note 05/11). Parallel thinking uses a generative aggregator. Gains over GLM 4.5 Air at N=20 range from +1.9 (FinanceBench) to +5.9 (TREC-Biogen), with diminishing returns beyond N=15. On PMBench with 5 rollouts, the aggregator beats every individual rollout 23.7% of the time. Value-guided search (Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 value model, k=2, N=17 trees, weighted majority vote) takes KARL-BCP from 59.6 to 70.4 on BrowseComp-Plus.
9. Behavior (note 08). Iter. 2 retrieves 37% more unique documents than base on BrowseComp-Plus (+8% on TREC-Biogen). Accuracy on 87 full-recall queries goes 53%→64%→71%, and searches go 91→52→32. Median BrowseComp-Plus trajectory is 20 steps in Iter. 2 versus 50 in Iter. 1 (Fig. 7).
10. Multi-agent/RAG relevance (note 11). The agent has a single vector-search tool. Chunk size and k are fixed per dataset (k ≤ 20) and the paper does not tune retrieval per task.

LIMITS
- Single tool (vector search) and closed corpora only. The authors list structured retrieval, code execution and sub-agents as future work.
- Only two tasks are trained on: BrowseComp-Plus and TREC-Biogen. The "OOD" tasks (FreshStack, FinanceBench, QAMPARI, PMBench) are the other four in the same suite.
- BrowseComp-Plus is evaluated on a 230-question calibrated subset, with a stated ±1 difference from the full set. PMBench is proprietary and has 57 questions.
- Nugget scoring uses LLM judges. The paper reports no seeds or confidence intervals on scores. Baselines were run on the authors' own harness, with the best config chosen per model.
- BrowseComp-Plus indexes only the first 512 tokens, which cover 86.5% of gold evidence, so this caps the score.
- Failure modes the authors concede: the "Giving Up Early" category increases. They suspect a spurious link between short traces and correctness. KARL also refused an arithmetic question instead of computing. Compression can be harmful (App. G case). The rule-based behavior classifier agrees with humans about 75% of the time.
- The OAPL-vs-GRPO advantage is asserted, not ablated here. The paper cites Ritter et al. 2026 for OAPL.
- Models like Opus 4.6 and GPT 5.2 are dated releases.

BUILDS ON: OAPL (Ritter et al. 2026), A*PO (Brantley et al. 2025), GRPO (Shao et al. 2024), Value-Guided Search (Wang et al. 2025), LMSys decontamination (Yang et al. 2023), Search-R1 (Jin et al. 2025), DR Tulu (Shao et al. 2025), parallel thinking (Zhao et al. 2025a; Wen et al. 2025), LATS (Zhou et al. 2024), BrowseComp-Plus (Chen et al. 2025), GLM-4.5 (Zeng et al. 2025).

CODE: none. Loss in Eq. 1, p8.

FIGURES: Fig 1 (p1) is the cost-quality and latency-quality Pareto plot. Fig 3 (p8) is the Stage II filtering pipeline. Fig 8 (p17) is the SFT-vs-RL bar chart. Fig 9 (p17) shows the iteration curves. Fig 10 (p18) shows the max@k curves. Fig 37 (p52) shows the data funnel counts.

PROBLEMS: Charts are garbled in the extraction, so values come from the text and Table 4. No embedded instructions found. Fig. 1 shows "84.5" without a label. The quote "Pareto-optimal" claim rests on the authors' own harness and prices.
